title: Stronger integrity comes at a cost
text: Stronger integrity comes at a cost Cost (Monetary / Performance Overhead) Security Coverage of the threat model Lower Higher Lower Higher Secure boot OS integrity at boot dm-verity Read-only storage integrity Byzantine agreement Execution + persistent storage Multiple compute replicas Qualitative comparison 4
notes:
People have been actively looking at this problem for decades and there have been a lot of security measures proposed over the years that address parts of the problem. If we look at these solutions, a clear trend emerges: the higher the amount of security measures the costlier it is. <The slide to have a scatterplot. X-axis: Security, Y-axis: Cost (Monetary/Performance Overhead)>

On one hand, secure boot guarantees your OS has not been tampered with, dm-verity checks the integrity of read-only devices. These are cheaper solutions but do not account for the full threat model. On the other hand, we have heavyweight mechanisms like Byzantine agreement. Integrity violations in both execution and persistent storage could be protected if there are all compute decisions are taken by an Byzantine agreement system and the storage layer is realized with a BFT consensus protocol. But this massively blows up the cost since now there needs to be multiple replicas of the same compute server.

notes:
<Reuse some of the existing slides> In recent years, applications have switched to using Trusted Execution Environments or TEEs for short for this purpose. TEEs are sandbox environments provided by CPU vendors like Intel's TDX, Arm's SEV-SNP etc that claim to protect the execution integrity of the application, by providing a cryptographic proof that the cloud providers are running the exact application they are supposed to be running. They also provide memory confidentiality so that if the cloud provider can't access the memory of the running application. With correct cryptographic infrastructure, this will prevent cloud providers from pretending to be the application and tampering with the data.

Authoring clarification: SEV-SNP is AMD's technology. Remote attestation authenticates measured software/platform state; isolation protects execution and memory. Bind an authenticated, encrypted channel to attestation to resist application impersonation and in-transit tampering. Attestation alone is not a proof of every runtime computation, nor a guarantee of persistent-storage freshness.
